primary_documentation.supports: The first key block represents basic connectivity; isotope and stereochemical information is elsewhere, and protonation is separately indicated. Standard InChI uses /t for tetrahedral parities, with + or - for assigned centres. Unknown and undefined both use ?. Wholly unassigned stereo is omitted. Atom numbers follow canonical formula numbering apart from H. Nitrogen has restricted stereochemistry support, so counting every SMILES @ is not a carbon-centre completeness test.

does not consider stereochemistry, isotopes etc.
primary_documentation.supports: The drug chirality field concerns dosing form and is curated for drugs and clinical candidates. It is not structure-assignment completeness. Virtual parents are registered entities that can lack their own hierarchy row. Connectivity searching disregards stereo and isotope distinctions; result records still need the whole-record component check.
page_meta supplies total count and continuation links. Field-specific startswith filtering is documented. Exact support for the molecule structure key is verified in the preserved live schema.

Official database and structure exports exist. No bulk export contents were acquired in this recovery, and their exact coverage has not been established. This is neither an established shortcut nor a blocker.

carbon_scope_reasoning: The seed formula C20H24N2O2 assigns canonical atom numbers 1–20 to carbon; its /t centres are 13,14,19,20. Its canonical SMILES independently marks four carbon CH centres. Every peer shares the actual basic layers, and reference.py checks all per-record carbon tag counts against the InChI assignments. No assertion about a fifth nitrogen centre is needed for this explicitly carbon-only task.
